text:
Maria (runtime): quick sync on a weird tail jitter after the last runtime tweak. not p99-wide, but intermittent 40-120ms spikes for a subset of tenants during lane rebalances.
Devon: saw the dashboard blips. looks tightly coupled to handoff windows.
Maria (runtime): yep. pattern: steady baseline, then 10-30s of jitter that coincides with tenant moves between lanes, then back to normal.
Lee: can you paste a short trace example?
Maria (runtime): putting a distilled trace here:
```
[09:41:10] req X enters lane-A
[09:41:11] hot-tenant Y moved -> lane-B
[09:41:11] lane-B batch-cut triggers kernel swap
[09:41:11] kvcache detach/attach -> pause ~85ms
[09:41:14] processing resumes
```
Sasha: that detach/attach during kernel swap is the culprit. moving a tenant invalidates local KV residency and forces a coldpath touching hardware resources.
Devon: two high-level mitigations: (A) reduce frequency of moving hot tenants, (B) make handoffs nonblocking (e.g., incremental attach/anchor ops).
Lee: we should instrument a "handoff_jitter" metric: sample per-tenant latency delta pre/post handoff and tag traces. lightweight sampling (1 in N) will keep cost low.
Maria (runtime): prototype config I'm trying:
```
handoff_jitter_sampling:
  rate: 0.1   # sample 10% of handoffs
  windows: [3s, 20s]
  emit: traces + histograms
```
Sasha: also worth classifying handoffs: graceful (drain then move) vs forceful (immediate rebind). behaviour differs and should map to policies.
Devon: idea: for graceful handoffs keep a tiny anchor on old lane until new lane warms kvcache. anchor = sub-ms noop traffic that keeps pages resident.
Lee: what's the cost? even micro-anchors consume batch slots. we need a fairness budget and per-GPU token accounting.
Maria (runtime): proposing a "handoff anchor pool": reserve M anchors per GPU, each anchor is a tiny op that counts toward shaping. anchor usage tracked and throttled; tenants consume from their internal budget.
Sasha: I can add a simulator flag --simulate-handoff-anchor that models anchor ops as +1 token and injects kernel-switch cost. helps evaluate benefit without deploying.
Devon: I'll run replays with and without anchors and measure tail improvements. share in #eng-runtime-playback.
Lee: I'll draft PromQL panels for handoff_jitter and an explainer card: median delta, 90/95 percentiles, handoff count.
Maria (runtime): eviction/fallback rules: if anchor pool exhausted, fall back to immediate move but emit an event. add adaptive refill: when cluster-wide jitter rises, increase anchor availability temporarily.
Sasha: plus a smoothing rule: delay moves if a tenant's short-term latency slope > threshold to avoid exacerbating hot churn. delay window bounded (e.g., up to 500ms or small number of batches).
Devon: tradeoff matrix: delaying moves increases latency for the moved tenant, anchors consume batch capacity that could increase latency elsewhere, and reserved lanes cost infra. different SLA tiers should pick different defaults.
Maria (runtime): suggested default mapping: free tier = no anchors, best-effort immediate moves; standard = limited anchors + adaptive smoothing; enterprise = reserved lanes or guaranteed anchor budget. document rollout and opt-in flags.
Lee: we should also surface a "hand_off_class" label in traces (graceful/forceful/anchor) for filtering.
Sasha: will start sampler PR today (hooks to emit handoff_jitter and labels). aim to land simulator and basic sampling this week.
Devon: I'll queue a replay job and link results. plan: baseline -> simulate anchors -> simulate anchors + smoothing -> evaluate.
infra-bot: deploy-bot: canary rollout 5% -> 25% scheduled at 13:00 UTC.
Maria (runtime): good. keep an eye on the canary and particularly handoff_jitter metric. alert if median delta > 30ms for any tenant cohort. :eyes:
Devon: noted. thanks folks.
